newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope recovering well after surgery-official.
newsitem.headline: Pope recovering well after surgery-official.

text.p: Pope John Paul is recovering well from surgery to remove his appendix and further post-operative tests have confirmed that he does not have a tumour, his doctors said in a statement on Wednesday.
The official medical bulletin, issued 24 hours after surgery, also said the Pope had got out of his bed and taken a short walk. He had no fever and was not in pain, it said.
The medical report said the Pope's blood pressure, heart rate, breathing and other vital signs were normal. He had begun taking liquid food and had spoken at length with his doctors, it said.
"The post-operative recovery of the Holy Father is proceeding regularly," the medical bulletin said.
Tuesday's operation at the Gemelli Hospital was accompanied by intense media speculation that the Pope, 76, may have another tumour. He had a colon tumour the size of an orange removed in 1992.

Wednesday's statement said final tests of tissue removed during surgery had confirmed the findings of initial post-operative analysis that no new tumour was present. It said another medical bulletin would be issued "in the next few days".
